Installation and setup

Source: vignettes/installation.Rmd
installation.Rmd

Installing birdnetR

Install the released version from CRAN:

install.packages("birdnetR")

or the development version from GitHub:

pak::pak("birdnet-team/birdnetR")

How Python is set up

You don’t need to install Python yourself. birdnetR uses reticulate::py_require(): the first time you use birdnetR, reticulate downloads Python and the birdnet Python package with uv and keeps them in a cache. The first setup takes a few minutes; later sessions reuse the cache and start within seconds.

The default installation contains ONNX Runtime and LiteRT. It runs BirdNET+ V3.0 and BirdNET V2.4, and custom TFLite classifiers trained on V2.4.

birdnet_sitrep() shows which Python and which birdnet version birdnetR uses (see Troubleshoot).

Extra downloads

Some models need TensorFlow or PyTorch on top of the default installation:

You load birdnetR installs Download
birdnet_load_perch() TensorFlow about 600 MB
birdnet_load(backend = "pb"), Raven exports TensorFlow about 600 MB
backend = "tf" with library = "tflite", or where LiteRT is not available (Intel Macs, Windows on ARM) TensorFlow about 600 MB
birdnet_load(backend = "pt") PyTorch several GB with GPU support (about 6 GB for AMD GPUs), much less for the CPU-only version

birdnetR installs these the first time you load such a model, even in the middle of an R session. That first load takes longer. The needs column of birdnet_list_models() shows which model needs what (see Models and backends).

On Linux, uv installs the CUDA build of PyTorch by default, which is several GB even if you have no GPU. To get the CPU-only build, run Sys.setenv(UV_TORCH_BACKEND = "cpu") before the first birdnetR call.

Download progress

uv draws progress bars only when R runs in a terminal. In RStudio, Positron and other IDE consoles, it prints one line when a large download starts and one when it ends, with nothing in between, for example:

Downloading torch (846.0MiB)
 Downloaded torch

A large download can take several minutes. To see the progress, do the first load in R running in a terminal. The download is cached, so your IDE sessions use it afterwards.

Intel Macs

birdnetR is not tested on Intel Macs. If something does not work there, please report it.

On Intel Macs, TensorFlow can only be added before Python starts. If you load a model that needs TensorFlow after Python has started (for example after loading another model), birdnetR stops with:

On Intel Macs, TensorFlow must be added before Python starts. Restart R and make this load your first birdnetR call.

Restart R and load the TensorFlow model first. Perch v2 does not run on Intel Macs at all.

Pinning the birdnet version

birdnetR installs the newest birdnet Python package from 1.5 up to, but not including, 2.0. To stay on one exact version, for example to reproduce earlier results, set the environment variable BIRDNETR_BIRDNET_VERSION before you load birdnetR, in your .Renviron file or with Sys.setenv():

Sys.setenv(BIRDNETR_BIRDNET_VERSION = "==1.5.0")
library(birdnetR)

Only an exact version of the form ==x.y.z is accepted. Anything else gives a warning and the default range is used.

Your own Python environment

If you set RETICULATE_PYTHON to the Python of your own virtual environment, birdnetR uses that environment and does not change it. This also means it can’t install the extras there. Install them yourself, for example with reticulate::virtualenv_install("my-env", "birdnet[tf]") for TensorFlow or "birdnet[pt]" for PyTorch. If a runtime is missing, the birdnet Python package stops with an error that names it.

RETICULATE_PYTHON must be set before Python starts: in your .Renviron file, or with Sys.setenv() before you load the first model. reticulate::use_virtualenv() alone does not work with birdnetR, because birdnetR sets RETICULATE_PYTHON to reticulate’s managed environment when it is unset, and RETICULATE_PYTHON takes precedence.

Some GPU setups need your own environment; see the GPU article.

Working offline

Models are downloaded the first time you load them. Run your analysis once while online, so that Python, the Python packages and the models are on disk.

When the environment variable BIRDNET_OFFLINE is 1, the birdnet Python package never tries to download anything. A model that is not on disk then stops with an error that names its download URL. Set the variable before you load a model:

Sys.setenv(BIRDNET_OFFLINE = "1")
model <- birdnet_load()
